in_run_pair_suppliers.interface: The actual finite-budget routine takes a metric space (X,d), self-map G:X→X, initial point, residual tolerance, and update budget; it returns residual-tolerance-met or budget-exhausted after at most N updates. It asserts no convergence or error bound, so this pair imports only its fixed-point iteration interface.

The rank-r domain is Hermitian idempotents with trace r; the eigenvalue Lipschitz item orders eigenvalues descending with multiplicity, converted by reversing indices for our ascending convention; the finite model assumes positive-definite overlap, Hermitian h, real-linear self-adjoint G, and real C2 E_xc on an open neighborhood. Its justified_by gradient proposition supplies F=h+G+∇E_xc; its actual hypotheses match the local examples.

external_page_requires.interface: The abstract Riesz-projection route is not imported: its actual definition requires Choice. The local block proof uses a finite Hermitian spectral expansion and scalar circle Cauchy formula, preserving the choice-free branch.
Completeness is used for the closed density-domain subset and for the abstract contraction theorem; Banach is applied only to a nonempty complete invariant set and a q-contraction with 0≤q<1.

The actual spectral theorem supplies unitary diagonalization and real eigenvalues; Weyl yields the batch-92 Hermitian eigenvalue Lipschitz bound; singular-value formulas give ||A||op≤||A||F. Spectral clusters are selected only across a strict rth gap; internal multiplicities are allowed.
The actual algorithm supplies only the finite-budget fixed-point update/status interface. No convergence or error result is inferred from the algorithm body.
The page and its actual item bodies supply the finite model and complex-projector conventions. Its other page-level claims are not imported.
